assumption_statement: Sponsors will pay about 20 bps a year on average billable AUA for outsourced DAF administration while keeping legal ownership and reserved decisions.
admissibility_result: Admissible as a hypothesis; inadmissible as a uniform price across balance bands (unbounded claim: per-account price varies 3x across targets).
operational_test: Fails under pressure at high balances: 20 bps = $2,221/account at top-25 median vs Ren $737; fails at low balances: $300/account at $150k is below every observed staffed price ($389+).
supporting_evidence: Ren/MS GIFT 18.5 bps (EV-PRC-003); TIFIN ADV 30 bps <=$1M (PRC O-028); Ren USCGT 40 bps (PRC O-008).
contradictory_evidence: Per-account market band $389-815 (PRC (b)); 20 bps fee = median 11-20% of target sponsors' whole non-investment opex (EV-ADV-004); Unbound EV-07 large sponsor margins, low switching pressure (EV-ADV-016).
evidence_admissibility_notes: All price points are incumbent payments with scope inferred from 990 labels; channel/captive prices (MS GIFT, RCF) are not arm's-length.
hidden_assumptions: Buyer thinks in bps; no tiering above $1M; scope equals Ren's; sponsor passes fee to donors unchanged.
causal_mechanism: Sponsor revenue is bps; a bps servicer fee shares it; WTP is capped by avoided internal cost + risk transfer, which scales with accounts and transactions, not assets.
alternative_explanations: Observed bps prices reflect bundling and channel economics; per-account cost drives real negotiations at high balances.
incentives: Servicer: favour high-balance books; sponsor: negotiate tiers/caps; incumbents: re-tier small accounts.
feedback_loops: High-balance wins get repriced at renewal toward per-account parity; low-balance wins lose money -> floor -> donor attrition.
failure_conditions: Median accepted effective price < $/account cost x 1.3, or tiers that cut effective bps below ~12 at $1M+ balances.
counterfactuals: $/account-year price with a declining bps tier; activity fees for tails.
falsifying_evidence: Three of five qualified sponsors refuse 20 bps flat on $1M+ average books, or accept only per-account pricing <= $800.
correctability: Moderate before signature; low within a multi-year contract
monitoring_signal: Accepted effective $/account and bps by balance band in discovery
edf_applicability: Not applicable: EDF step 2 needs an observed outcome; the servicer does not exist. Only claim-state vocabulary and evidence separation used.
edf_adjacent_observed_outcome: Ren's realised 18.5 bps at MS GIFT is below the 27 bps first donor tier (why: concentration, custom tiers or sharing) - EDF-1 candidate
recommended_commitment: Continue Experiment (price discovery by balance band)
adv_conclusion_would_flip: Yes: '20 bps credible for $250k+ programs' and '20 single-sponsor sustainers'
adv_flip_condition: Buyers cap at a per-account price near $737 (or lower)

assumption_statement: A five-person fixed core can run the servicer.
admissibility_result: Admissible; the F# model already adds 1 minimum ops FTE, so the live structure is 6.
operational_test: Fails on absence and December: single releaser pair; controller counted as preparer (ADV-023).
supporting_evidence: CST Model B costing; ACT core absorbs ~1,600 h.
contradictory_evidence: ACT: 3-4 added hires at 5,000 accounts; ~10 FTE-eq in December; prior AI-native model 24 FTE at 1,000 accounts (assumption).
evidence_admissibility_notes: All staffing numbers are assumptions from one programme.
hidden_assumptions: Platform exists; sponsor makes reserved decisions; no 24x7 on-call; founder does sales, compliance and incidents.
causal_mechanism: Fixed accountability roles plus variable hours at 1,520 h/FTE.
alternative_explanations: Leanness produced by Burden Externalization to sponsor and Echelon.
incentives: Founders understate fixed cost to reach break-even.
failure_conditions: Any day without two qualified releasers; SOC 1 SoD exception.
counterfactuals: Model C (12 core) or outsourced operations partner.
falsifying_evidence: Roster simulation with leave and December showing coverage gaps at 6 people.
threshold: Any coverage gap; >5% items past SLA
trigger_claim: A coverage gap is a control failure, not a delay
edf_applicability: Not applicable: EDF step 2 needs an observed outcome; the servicer does not exist. Only claim-state vocabulary and evidence separation used.
edf_adjacent_observed_outcome: 0-employee sponsors whose affiliates do the work (MS GIFT, Fidelity) - where staffing cost actually sits
recommended_commitment: Delay hiring plan until roster simulation
adv_conclusion_would_flip: Partly: Model B break-even rises ~$0.07B with utilisation alone
adv_flip_condition: Utilisation 0.85 and controller excluded from preparation

assumption_statement: Incremental cost is about $75 per fund-year above the fixed budget.
admissibility_result: Flag: tidy single number; ACT replaced it with archetype drivers.
operational_test: Fails for high-frequency, high-value, complex archetypes (2-7x).
supporting_evidence: ACT activity model; CST vendor prices.
contradictory_evidence: No time study anywhere (EV-ACT-029); cost per grant $55-$419 across sponsors.
hidden_assumptions: Mix 20/20/40/7/10/3 applies to every sponsor; workload invariant to balance (ADV-009).
causal_mechanism: Labour minutes x rate + per-transaction fees.
alternative_explanations: Per-account cost proxies activity; equal-account sponsors differ several-fold.
feedback_loops: Unpriced tails grow if onboarding is indiscriminate.
edf_applicability: Not applicable: EDF step 2 needs an observed outcome; the servicer does not exist. Only claim-state vocabulary and evidence separation used.
adv_conclusion_would_flip: Yes for small-sponsor viability; no for high-balance books

assumption_statement: Automation keeps human handling low enough for lean staffing.
admissibility_result: Admissible only for eligibility reuse; the model applies AI-native minutes from day one (ADV-003), which is inadmissible under Unbound EV-08.
operational_test: Fails before delegations exist; fails if sponsor requires per-grant sign-off.
contradictory_evidence: EV-08 activation gates; EV-02 levers unmeasured; 12/100 sanctions misses in replay.
evidence_admissibility_notes: Replay = Schedule I recipient rows, not grants.
hidden_assumptions: Board delegation at go-live; auditor acceptance; incumbents do not copy.
alternative_explanations: Savings come from policy (EFT default, deferral), not AI.
feedback_loops: A miss tightens rules and lowers automation.
falsifying_evidence: Shadow replay + time study at a design partner.
monitoring_signal: Human touches per 1,000 accounts; delegation date
edf_applicability: Not applicable: EDF step 2 needs an observed outcome; the servicer does not exist. Only claim-state vocabulary and evidence separation used.
edf_adjacent_observed_outcome: Replay: 12 of 100 perturbed listed names passed the reference matcher
recommended_commitment: Continue Experiment; model AI-enhanced as base until measured
adv_conclusion_would_flip: Yes: capital ($3.40M -> $4.32M anchor) and every break-even
adv_flip_condition: Redesign levers not active for 12+ months

admissibility_result: Inadmissible as a plan input without a named, dated trigger.

alternative_explanations: Large sponsors re-platform with software vendors, not servicers.
incentives: Anchor demands price concessions and MFN.
feedback_loops: Anchor concentration -> pricing power to anchor.
falsifying_evidence: Zero qualified sponsors with a dated trigger in 15-20 interviews.
trigger_claim: Then runway cannot reach first revenue

incentives: Sponsors exclude cash or large accounts from base.

assumption_statement: The servicer stays outside custody, advice and fundraising regulation.
admissibility_result: Admissible as design rule; not a legal conclusion.
operational_test: Fails if payment initiation is treated as money transmission or marketing as solicitation.
supporting_evidence: Design rule; Ren/TIFIN operate similar models.
alternative_explanations: Sponsors' banks may refuse third-party initiation.
feedback_loops: Centralised rails cut cost but add licensing.

assumption_statement: Contracts carry minimum annual fees covering fixed cost in ramp and downturns.
working_value: Not set; break-even minimum $60k-$565k for small sponsors (results.md)
operational_test: Fails if anchor negotiates no minimum.
supporting_evidence: USBFS $60k fund-admin minimum; Ren/Stellar flat $118-175k floors (PRC (d)).
causal_mechanism: Minimum converts variable revenue to fixed.
alternative_explanations: Minimums shift risk to donors via sponsor fees.
feedback_loops: Minimum -> sponsor raises donor fees -> attrition.
edf_applicability: Not applicable: EDF step 2 needs an observed outcome; the servicer does not exist. Only claim-state vocabulary and evidence separation used.
edf_adjacent_observed_outcome: Ren/Stellar small-client lines flat across years

assumption_statement: A per-account floor (e.g. $250/yr) is a fair and acceptable way to make small funds viable.
admissibility_result: Inadmissible as '20 bps' framing: the effective price is 24-45 bps (EV-ADV-002).
operational_test: Fails for small/dormant funds: $250 on $1,368 is 18%/yr; on $3,420 7.3%/yr.
contradictory_evidence: Those are donor-facing totals; a servicer floor plus sponsor margin stacks above them.
evidence_admissibility_notes: Floor applied to rescaled archetype balances (ADV-009) exaggerates the tail; real distribution unknown.
hidden_assumptions: Sponsor absorbs or passes floor; donors do not close funds.
causal_mechanism: Cost is per account; floor aligns revenue with cost.
alternative_explanations: Dormant funds should be swept to charity under sponsor policy rather than charged.
incentives: Floor rewards keeping many small funds open.
feedback_loops: High minimum -> small donors leave -> fewer accounts, lower cost but lower access.
failure_conditions: Floor > 2% of balance for >10% of funds.
counterfactuals: Floor capped at 1% of balance; dormant-fund sweep; activity fees instead.
falsifying_evidence: Balance distribution of a target sponsor.
monitoring_signal: Share of funds paying floor; floor as % balance
edf_applicability: Not applicable: EDF step 2 needs an observed outcome; the servicer does not exist. Only claim-state vocabulary and evidence separation used.

assumption_statement: Asset-based servicer fees do not create material incentives against charitable outcomes (delaying grants, retaining assets, rejecting complex gifts, minimum fees).
admissibility_result: Unbounded; must be stated per incentive.
operational_test: Partly fails: direct $ incentive to delay is tiny ($1.64 per $10k grant-month) but cost incentive (December deferral) and fee-base incentive (retention, sweep resistance) are real.
supporting_evidence: Sponsor retains grant decisions; servicer does not decide.
contradictory_evidence: ACT recommends 10-day December SLA to save staff; complex gift cost $358 + 359 min with no fee.
hidden_assumptions: Servicer has no influence on sponsor policy.
causal_mechanism: Revenue tied to AUA; cost tied to grants.
alternative_explanations: Sponsors already have the same incentive (bps donor fees).
incentives: Servicer and sponsor both benefit from retention.
feedback_loops: Payout up -> revenue down, workload up -> pressure on SLAs.
failure_conditions: Grant latency or complex-gift refusals rise after outsourcing.
counterfactuals: Payout-neutral pricing; fee base excluding approved-unpaid grants.
falsifying_evidence: Grant latency and payout before/after at a client.
monitoring_signal: Median approval-to-payment days; payout rate; complex-gift acceptance rate
trigger_claim: Servicer economics are shaping charitable flows
edf_applicability: Not applicable: EDF step 2 needs an observed outcome; the servicer does not exist. Only claim-state vocabulary and evidence separation used.

admissibility_result: Admissible as arithmetic; inadmissible as a general claim (scope and balance-bound).

incentives: Channel owner prices admin low to protect advisory.
